name: scan-still-running
description: The scan is queued and has not run, which is the state every run passes through and the one the delete used to fire in. `PUT .../scan` answers with a task in status `new` -- queued, not started -- and the task keeps reporting `new` on every check. The passive asset is the ONLY record this host exists: delete it now and a device that turns out to be offline, unreachable, or whose scan errors is erased with nothing to show it was ever there. So no bulk delete may be issued, and `requests_absent` on it is the assertion this scenario exists for. `scan_wait_seconds` is 0 so the run does not sit here for the default half hour -- the parameter's own contract is 'check once, do not wait', and this is what it looks like. The two log lines are what separate this from a run that aborted or returned early: both are printed after the wait gave up, and neither is reachable any other way. The assets stay, and the next run finds them again and queues another scan; that is the cost of the safe direction, and it is far cheaper than a deleted host. delete_assets is passed explicitly because deletion now ships OFF by default (unresolved question of the scan merging onto the passive asset it supersedes).

log_contains: Gave up waiting for 1 scan task(s) after 0s; keeping their assets for a later run
No scan completed in time; keeping every passive asset for a later run
